concept.name: Scaling out
concept.definition: Closing a position in partial tranches at successively more favorable prices rather than exiting all at once, banking profits progressively while leaving a residual position to capture further movement.
concept.intuition: Selling a third at each target converts an all-or-nothing exit into a ladder: some profit is locked in, and the remaining runner is effectively financed by realized gains.
concept.mechanics: Predefine partial-exit levels or targets; as each is reached, close a fraction of the position and commonly move the stop on the remainder to break-even or better, so the residual position carries little remaining downside relative to the entry.
concept.formula: Remaining size after k exits = Q_0 - sum(q_i); realized P&L = sum(q_i x (p_i - p_entry)) over exited tranches i.
concept.failure_modes: In strong trends scaling out caps participation in the biggest moves - the residual runner earns a fraction of what full size would have; in choppy markets premature partials plus tightened stops can exit the whole position at the worst moments.
concept.misconceptions: That scaling out is always the prudent choice; its main documented benefit is psychological and risk-smoothing, and fixed full exits can outperform staggered ones when trends persist.
concept.example: Holding 900 shares from a $50 entry, sell 300 at $52 and 300 at $54, move the stop to $50, and let the last 300 run - $1,200 is banked while upside exposure remains.
